title: Khajuraho and the Nagara Temple

endcard.line: Pictures: Arnold Betten; Ms Sarah Welch (public domain, CC0); Radosław Botev (CC BY 3.0)

segments.say: This temple is built to look like a mountain. Peak rises behind peak, climbing to a summit, like the Himalaya.
These are the temples of Khajuraho, built by the Chandela kings around a thousand years ago. Of perhaps eighty-five, about twenty-five survive.

anim.title: The Nagara style (north India)
items: Halls lead in to the sanctum

segments.say: They are the finest example of the Nagara style of north India: a high platform, halls leading inward, and a curved tower, the shikhara, with smaller towers stacked against it.
The largest is the Kandariya Mahadeva temple, dedicated to Shiva. Its tower carries dozens of miniature towers.

left.title: Nagara (north)
items: Tower over the sanctum is tallest

segments.say: Compare it with the Dravida style of the south: a stepped, pyramid-shaped tower called a vimana, inside a walled compound with gateways.
The walls are covered with carvings of gods, dancers, musicians and daily life, a celebration of the whole world.
For GS One: Khajuraho, the Chandelas, and the Nagara temple shaped like a mountain.
